description: Counts, from the BrainChain MCP dataset, of how often one kind of public step of a Robinhood Chain token was followed by a venue listing the token: of the tokens that took the step, how many were listed within 7, 30 and 90 days after it, or within `within` days. These are counts of what happened before, with the tokens behind each: they give no score and say nothing of what happens next. A step does not say why a venue listed a token, and most tokens with any of these steps are never listed. Pass the kind as `trace`: `pool` (a first Uniswap pool), `custody_pr` (a pull request adding it to BitGo's code), `custody` (BitGo's merge of it into its Robinhood Chain tokens), `custody_release` (the first @bitgo/statics release with it), `listing_pr` (a pull request adding it to Trust Wallet's or MetaMask's list), `listing` (Trust Wallet's or MetaMask's merge of it into their lists), `aggregator` (LI.FI or CoinGecko listing it), `approval` (a followed market maker wallet's first approval of it), `pool_queued` (a market maker's multisig queuing one of its pools), `announcement` (an exchange's announcement naming it). A kind brainchain_changes reports, such as bitgo.merged, is taken as the step it records. `n` is how many tokens took the step, and `undated` how many took it with no date the source gives, which counts in no window. Each of `windows` gives `days`, `steps`, the tokens whose step came a full window before the cut-off, and `outcomes`: `any` venue, and each one: `robinhood_page` (a page in Robinhood's crypto sitemap), `robinhood_tradable` (a tradable pair in the list Robinhood serves to API clients), `kucoin` (KuCoin listing it on Robinhood Chain), `gate` (Gate listing it on Robinhood Chain), `kraken` (Kraken's post that it is available for trading), `binance_futures` (a futures market on Binance Futures), `upbit` (a market on Upbit), `bithumb` (a market on Bithumb), `bitget` (a market on Bitget). Each count gives `before`, the tokens the venue had listed before the step, which are left out; `eligible`, the rest; `unknown`, eligible tokens the venue lists without a date for it, which cannot be placed inside or outside the window; `followed`, those listed within the window; `share`, `followed` over `eligible` less `unknown`; `medianLeadDays` from the step to the listing; and `tokens`, the contract addresses behind `followed`, `unknown` and `before`. KuCoin and Gate are matched by the contract they list on Robinhood Chain and dated by the trading start each publishes. Binance Futures, Upbit, Bithumb and Bitget count from their first market for the token, read from the market lists each publishes: matched by the contract the exchange gives for the asset on Robinhood Chain, as Bitget does, or else by its own name for it, as Upbit and Bithumb give, and dated by the time the exchange gives the market, as Binance Futures and Bitget do, or else by when BrainChain's watcher first saw it. A market already there when the watcher first read the exchange is listed by that time when the exchange's contract ties it to the token, and is left out when only a symbol or a name does. Binance Futures gives neither a contract nor a name, so its markets rest on the symbol. Kraken counts from its blog post that the token is available for trading, dated by the post, which can come days after trading opened. Robinhood publishes no contract and no date: it is matched by symbol, confirmed by Robinhood's own name for the asset in its pair list or on its page, and dated by when BrainChain's watcher first saw it, so a listing already there when the watcher started on November 19, 2026 counts as `before` for a step after that day and as `unknown` for one before it. A listing with nothing to confirm it but the symbol is left out of every count, since a token on Robinhood Chain can call itself by another asset's symbol: `unconfirmed` gives how many such rows the tokens with this step have, and `tokens`, which tokens. Bitstamp is not counted: its robots.txt closes its API to automated clients, so the daily build does not read it; brainchain_token_sightings still reads it when asked. A pool counts once the stretch of 10,000 blocks it was created in had ended; every token with a pool is counted, those that were never listed too. To count only what was public at a point in the past, pass `at`, a time in ISO 8601 such as 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z, or `atBlock`: each row counts from the time its source dates it. `cut` gives the time used. `venue` keeps one venue: robinhood (both of its sources), robinhood_page, robinhood_tradable, kucoin, gate, kraken, binance_futures, upbit, bithumb, bitget. `dataset` names what was read: its `date`, the `headBlock` it reaches, `readAt` and `manifest`, the SHA-256 of that day's manifest, which BrainChain inscribes on its chain; every file read is checked against the manifest first. The dataset is built once a day by `brainchain-mcp dataset` and read from its public repository, or from the directory or address BRAINCHAIN_DATASET names. Counts appear once a dataset has been published there: until then, or while it cannot be read, the tool says so and counts nothing. Free, no key and no payment. Not advice.

at.description: Optional: a time in ISO 8601. Only rows public by then are counted.

atBlock.description: Optional, in place of at: a block number. Only rows public by the end of that block are counted.

trace.description: The kind of step, such as custody or bitgo.merged.

venue.description: Optional: one venue to count, in place of all of them.

within.description: Optional: one window, in days, in place of 7, 30 and 90.

name: brainchain_trace_outcomes
title: How often a kind of public step was followed by a listing
